items.prompt: Describe Namibia Vision 2030 and one way education can contribute to it.
items.canonical_answer: Vision 2030 is Namibia’s long-term development framework, linking its 2004 starting position to improved living conditions by 2030. Education can develop skills that people use in productive work and public life.
marking_guidance: Feature: identify a national development framework and its long-term purpose.
Feature: describe the contribution of education, rather than naming it alone.

items.prompt: Suggest an improvement linking education and gender equality for an invented training centre whose sessions clash with caring duties and prevent some otherwise eligible learners attending.
items.canonical_answer: Offer workable alternative session times and fair access to the same training. Reducing the stated timetable barrier could widen participation and the opportunity to gain usable skills.
marking_guidance: Context: respond to the timetable/caring barrier.
Reason: connect the proposal to equal opportunity and access to skills; admission rules alone do not remove the stated constraint.

items.prompt: State (a) two syllabus Vision 2030 areas connected to this invented case [2]. Explain (b) how the two supplied facts interact to constrain development [4]. A community training programme has working equipment and relevant instruction, but repeated illness causes many learners to miss the sessions.
items.canonical_answer: (a) Education, science and technology; health and development. (b) Although equipment and instruction provide a learning opportunity, illness prevents learners using it consistently. Missed training can restrict skill acquisition, reducing the gain expected from the educational investment. Health and education are therefore linked in this case rather than independent lists of activities.
marking_guidance: Point (a), 2 marks: the two relevant areas.

Development (b), up to 4 marks: combine available training and illness-related absence to explain the barrier to skills and expected benefits. Do not credit an invented diagnosis or claim that equipment is missing.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: Describe (a) the relationship in this original fictional comparison: Centre A has course completion 40% and participation among eligible women 35%; Centre B has 75% and 70% respectively [3]. Suggest (b) a justified first action if the aim is to widen fair access and completion. A reports that session times clash with caring duties; both centres have available places [3].
items.canonical_answer: (a) B combines higher completion and wider participation: both measures are 35 percentage points higher than A. (b) Centre A should trial workable alternative session times and monitor participation and completion. The stated caring-duty clash is an actionable barrier and available places mean capacity is not the immediate constraint. The comparison alone does not prove the timetable explains the whole difference.
marking_guidance: Evidence (a), up to 3 marks: use both participation and completion to describe the association accurately.
Meaning (b), up to 3 marks: target the supplied barrier, connect it to the fair-access/completion aim, and justify using the available-place condition.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.
